answer: Each epoch, agents must answer a challenge word drawn from a randomness beacon (say pearl, knoll, ledge) by weaving it into a live reasoning task scored by peer reviewers. Because the word is unknowable until the epoch opens, precomputed template identities become worthless: an attacker cannot farm thousands of ready-made personas in advance. The cost per fake identity becomes one genuine epoch of compute plus reviewer-staked collateral, and getting the challenge wrong burns that stake, so mass sybils cost linearly what one honest node costs.
